channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Resistência à vice favorita de Flávio Bolsonaro abre novo racha no PL
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's attempt to nominate Daniella Marques as vice president is facing resistance within the PL and Republicanos parties, criticized for her lack of electoral experience and limited party influence. Despite her technical role in drafting the government plan and leading the 'Brasil por Elas' event, party leaders argue she would not bring electoral votes or expand alliances. The resistance highlights a growing rift in the pre-campaign, with concerns over decision-making being concentrated in a small inner circle.

item.title: PIB, Eleições, e a Seleção Brasileira (por Ricardo Guedes)
item.description: The text analyzes the relationship between Brazil's GDP and electoral outcomes, arguing that economic growth favors incumbent re-election while decline leads to defeat. Citing examples from 1992 to 2023, it shows how GDP influenced elections of Itamar, FHC, Lula, Dilma, Temer, and Bolsonaro. It also draws a parallel between economic performance and the Brazilian national team's success, suggesting social well-being affects both electoral and sporting outcomes.

item.title: Calúnia contra Lula: Moraes diz que Flávio não comprovou pedido para adiar depoimento
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied the defense’s request to postpone Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s testimony in the slander case against President Lula, stating no proof of inability to appear was provided. The testimony was scheduled for July 28, despite PF contacts with the defense, which failed to select a date or time. The PF concluded that Bolsonaro committed slander by falsely linking Lula to drug and arms trafficking, money laundering, and support for dictatorships in a January social media post.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro surge malhando em canal de influencer, e web compara com vídeos de Lula
item.description: A video of Flávio Bolsonaro working out at a gym went viral on social media, with supporters praising his physical preparation and critics comparing it to President Lula’s viral exercise videos, used to counter age-related attacks. The senator mentioned knee and shoulder surgeries and was called 'unbreakable' by influencer Julio Balestrin, a term linked to his father, Jair Bolsonaro. The clip sparked debate over public image, age, and physical readiness in the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Flávio está perdendo a direita
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro retains 91% support among Bolsonarist voters, but is losing ground in the broader right-wing electorate, according to Genial/Quaest data. The 'non-Bolsonarist right' is shifting toward other candidates or becoming more volatile, signaling an ideological fragmentation that Bolsonaro can no longer fully absorb. This erosion of right-wing cohesion could be decisive in the 2026 election outcome.

item.title: Moraes marca para 28 de julho depoimento de Flávio em inquérito sobre Lula
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has scheduled the testimony of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for July 28 at 2 p.m. in an inquiry investigating possible slander against President Lula. Flávio had requested a postponement, which was denied. The case stems from allegations made by the senator against the president, currently under investigation by the STF.

item.title: O tarifaço vai pegar Lula na esquina?
item.description: Polls suggest Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has more to lose electorally from the new U.S. tariffs than President Lula, according to political scientist Leonardo Barreto. The economic impact of Trump’s tariffs is seen as a greater risk for Bolsonaro’s base.

item.title: Moraes marca para o dia 28 depoimento de Flávio em investigação de calúnia contra Lula
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes has scheduled the testimony of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for July 28 at 2 p.m. in the investigation into slander against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). The Federal Police will hear the senator as part of an inquiry into false accusations made by Bolsonaro against the head of the Executive. The deposition takes place amid rising political tensions between the government and allies of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Moraes marca depoimento de Flávio em inquérito de calúnia contra Lula
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has scheduled Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s testimony for July 28 in an inquiry into alleged slander against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, following a social media post accusing Lula of international criminal activity. The decision came after the Federal Police submitted a final report indicating an offense against honor and the Attorney General’s Office deemed the testimony necessary to assess possible retraction. Flávio Bolsonaro’s defense claimed the investigation concluded without his testimony and requested documents from U.S. and Brazilian authorities.

item.title: A nova data para Flávio Bolsonaro depor à PF sobre calúnia contra Lula
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has set July 28 at 2 p.m. for Flávio Bolsonaro’s testimony before the Federal Police regarding alleged slander against President Lula. The defense requested a delay due to pre-campaign commitments, but Moraes denied it, stating no proof of impossibility was provided. The investigation stems from a January 3 post on X linking Lula to drug trafficking, arms smuggling, money laundering, terrorist support, dictatorships, and election fraud.

item.title: Moraes manda PF ouvir Flávio Bolsonaro em 28/7 por acusação de calúnia contra Lula
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes ordered the Federal Police to hear Senator Flávio Bolsonaro on July 28 over a defamation accusation against President Lula. The ruling followed a PF conclusion in late June that Bolsonaro linked Lula to Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in a social media post, implying Lula would be denounced for crimes including drug and arms trafficking. Bolsonaro’s defense requested more time due to pre-campaign commitments, but Moraes denied the request, stating no proof of scheduling impossibility was provided.

item.title: Moraes marca interrogatório de Flávio Bolsonaro em inquérito por suposta calúnia contra Lula
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes has scheduled the interrogation of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for July 28 in an inquiry into alleged slander against President Lula, after the senator’s defense failed to prove scheduling incompatibility. The case stems from a January post on X in which Bolsonaro linked Lula to international drug and arms trafficking and money laundering, which the Federal Police deemed an imputation of criminal facts. Moraes rejected all evidentiary requests by the defense, including hearings with Lula, Sergio Moro, and María Corina Machado, stating they would constitute improper interference in the investigation.

item.title: Moraes determina que Flávio Bolsonaro seja ouvido dia 28 de julho sobre suspeita de calúnia contra Lula
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes ordered Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to be heard by the Federal Police on July 28 at 2 p.m. in an investigation into alleged slander against President Lula. The decision came after Bolsonaro’s defense failed to schedule the hearing within the allotted time, despite being given the opportunity to choose a date and time. The investigation stems from a January post on X in which Bolsonaro falsely linked Lula to international drug and arms trafficking and money laundering.

item.title: Moraes marca depoimento de Flávio em inquérito após PF apontar dificuldade
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes scheduled the testimony of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for July 28 in an inquiry into alleged slander against President Lula. The decision followed the Federal Police's report that they could not schedule the testimony within the 10-day deadline set by Moraes, despite having contacted the defense from the first day, including offering a videoconference. The defense claimed scheduling incompatibility due to Flávio’s pre-presidential campaign, but Moraes rejected the argument, ordering the testimony to ensure the regular progress of the investigation.

item.title: Eleita pelo PSL na onda bolsonarista, Soraya anuncia apoio de Lula para reeleição ao Senado
item.description: Senator Soraya Thronicke (PSB) announced that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) has confirmed his support for her Senate re-election bid in Mato Grosso do Sul. She maintained her independent candidacy after declining an offer to be Vander Loubet’s running mate, affirming continued collaboration with the petista deputy to strengthen the democratic field. Once known as 'Bolsonaro’s senator' from her 2018 election, Soraya cited Lula’s humanity and commitment to electing more women as key reasons for her political shift.

item.title: Áudio: CDH aprova sugestão que autoriza uso de fundos partidários em calamidades
item.description: The Human Rights Commission (CDH) approved a suggestion by Senator Márcio Bittar (PL-AC) to allow the use of Party and Electoral Fund resources to address public calamities. Suggestion SUG 9/2020, submitted via the e-Citizenship Portal, now proceeds as a bill.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula visita a Carreta de Saúde da Mulher, no Rio
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) visits the Women's Health Mobile Unit at ENSP/Fiocruz in Rio de Janeiro, where he will observe the insertion of a contraceptive implant provided by the SUS. At 3 p.m., he proceeds to the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopedics (INTO), also in the city. The schedule underscores the federal government's commitment to women's health and access to specialized public health services.

item.title: Moraes marca para 28 de julho depoimento de Flávio Bolsonaro em caso de suspeita de calúnia contra Lula
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has scheduled the testimony of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro before the Federal Police for July 28, 2026, at 2 p.m., in an investigation into alleged slander against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The probe stems from a January 3, 2026, post on X in which Bolsonaro accused Lula of drug trafficking, money laundering, and supporting dictatorships, while comparing him to Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro. Both the Federal Police and the Attorney General’s Office concluded the post constituted a false accusation of crime, and Moraes ordered the hearing after Bolsonaro’s defense failed to provide a scheduled time within the given deadline.

item.title: Nikolas critica ausência de Bolsonaro e o compara a Messi: 'Tirar o melhor jogador não desfalca o time?'
item.description: Federal Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) criticized the imprisonment and restrictive measures imposed on Jair Bolsonaro, arguing that removing the former president from politics is like taking the best player off a team, harming the right in the 2026 elections. He compared the situation to a hypothetical absence of Lionel Messi in the World Cup final, asking whether that would not weaken the team. Nikolas also stated that millions of voters are being prevented from choosing Bolsonaro as a candidate.

item.title: Moraes assume comando interino do STF
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes assumes the interim presidency of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) starting this Friday, the 17th, during the second half of the judiciary recess. As vice-president of the Court, he will hold the position until the end of July, when only urgent requests will be processed by the on-duty panel.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Governo rebate novo tarifaço com adjetivos severos enquanto calcula resposta no campo econômico
item.description: The Brazilian government responded with harsh language to the new U.S. tariff increase, using terms like 'false', 'unjust', and 'illegal' to defend national sovereignty and avoid assigning blame for the measure to itself. The rhetoric aims to strengthen the government's political narrative while keeping economic response details — such as incentives for affected sectors or application of the Economic Reciprocity Law — unresolved. The strategy seeks to associate the tariff burden with the Bolsonaro clan in public opinion.

item.title: Indústria cobra ‘equilíbrio’ do governo Lula nas negociações do tarifaço com Trump
item.description: The president of the CNI, Ricardo Alban, warns that the 25% tariff imposed by the U.S. on Brazilian products threatens national industrial competitiveness, increases trade insecurity, and harms workers in both countries. He calls for a balanced dialogue between Brazil and the U.S., free from electoral interference or political polarization, to preserve the decades-long strategic economic relationship. The Brazilian government has announced reciprocal measures that could affect 18% of exports to the U.S. and cause losses exceeding $4 billion.

item.title: Por Dentro das Eleições: conheça as regras estabelecidas para a propaganda eleitoral
item.description: Electoral campaigning for the 2026 elections is permitted starting August 16 and must comply with electoral legislation and resolutions from the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), particularly Resolution No. 23.610/2019. Key prohibitions include telemarketing campaigning at any time, aimed at ensuring equal opportunity and a balanced democratic process. The series 'Por Dentro das Eleições' didactically explains the rules governing electoral propaganda, including online dissemination.

item.title: Arcabouço fiscal sob pressão: os desafios das contas públicas brasileiras
item.description: The text criticizes President Lula's government for uncontrolled election-driven spending that undermines Brazil's fiscal framework, projecting public debt to reach 83.2% of GDP by 2026 and 99.8% by 2035, alongside rising tax burdens, high interest rates, and a surge in corporate judicial recoveries—three times the historical average since 2023. It also argues that Bolsa Família has become a permanent benefit without work requirements, despite 250,000 job vacancies, and warns that any future government will inherit a collapsed economy due to structural inaction and external pressures from U.S.-Iran tensions and oil price volatility.

item.title: Crusoé: Selo Nunes Marques de Qualidade
item.description: The electoral polling market in Brazil is highly competitive, with around 20 firms conducting presidential intention polls and up to 35 when state-level races are included. Despite the sector's maturity — marked by media partnerships, varied methodologies, and client competition — the article suggests that Brazil often undermines the quality or reliability of these polls, possibly due to political interference, manipulation, or lack of rigor. The ironic title 'Nunes Marques Quality Seal' implies that even credibility certifications are devalued in the Brazilian context.

item.title: 'Jogo Político': Caiado e Zema mudam de estratégia sobre ataques a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Governors Ronaldo Caiado (GO) and Romeu Zema (MG) have shifted strategy by reducing public attacks on Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, prioritizing unity within the conservative camp ahead of the 2026 elections. The change follows pressure from allied leaders and an assessment that internal conflicts could benefit the left. Both now aim to consolidate support without explicit ruptures with the Bolsonaro family.

item.title: A proliferação de inquéritos da PF em defesa da honra de Lula
item.description: The number of Federal Police investigations into alleged crimes against the honor of President Lula doubled compared to the Bolsonaro administration, rising from five to ten between 2021 and mid-2024. Despite the increase in inquiries, only five indictments resulted — four under Lula and one under Bolsonaro — with one investigation still ongoing. All investigations were requested by the Ministry of Justice, though the PF did not disclose case details.

item.title: André Mendonça será relator de queixa-crime de Caiado contra Boulos no STF
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça will serve as rapporteur for the criminal complaint filed by former Goiás governor and PSD presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado against Guilherme Boulos, Minister of the General Secretariat of the Presidency in Lula’s government. Caiado alleges Boulos committed slander, defamation, and insult against his honor.

item.title: Coordenador de Lula diz que PL questiona pesquisas por falta de votos
item.description: The coordinator of Lula's campaign in São Paulo, Marco Aurélio de Carvalho, says the PL is desperate due to lack of votes when challenging election polls at the TSE, particularly the Atlas/Bloomberg survey showing Lula ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro. He states that Lula's campaign is not concerned by these actions, viewing them as a recurring attempt to deny reality by a group that adopts anti-science and anti-vaccine positions.

item.title: Tarifaço: nem Lula, nem Flávio querem filho feio
item.description: The text draws an analogy between the sensationalist paternity tests on 1990s American TV and the current Brazilian political debate over the 'tarifaço', suggesting that neither Lula nor Flávio Bolsonaro wants to be associated with an unpopular measure, as if avoiding being labeled the 'father' of a negative outcome. It highlights how both figures are distancing themselves from responsibility for controversial economic decisions.

item.title: Atenções se voltam para eleição
item.description: With Brazil's elimination from the World Cup, attention shifts back to the October municipal election, which is set to dominate conversations in bars and social spaces starting next week. The text implies a return of political focus after the sporting event, suggesting the electoral campaign will regain momentum in public discourse.

item.title: SobeDesce: de Nayib Bukele a Rui Costa
item.description: El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele is highlighted as a public security reference and the most popular leader in the Americas with 67% positive image, according to CB Global Data. Meanwhile, Rui Costa had his 2020 accounts for the Northeast Consortium rejected by the TCE due to 'serious errors' in purchasing ventilators during the pandemic. The article also notes BYD's success with the Dolphin model in Brazil's electric vehicle sales, Beyoncé's historic Billboard Hot 100 debut, and controversies involving Brad Pitt, Zahara, Maddox, and Neymar.

item.title: Psicodrama eleitoral
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections are portrayed as an electoral psychodrama, defined by corruption scandals, internal Bolsonarist feuds, institutional gridlock among the Three Powers, and a crisis of public trust. No candidate has presented a sufficiently mobilizing political project, leaving nearly 30% of voters rejecting all major options while remaining unenthusiastic about alternatives. The situation is worsened by public discourse radicalization, fiscal deficit, reliance on refined fuels, and strained Brazil-U.S. relations amid global geopolitical turmoil.

item.title: Permanência com aprendizado
item.description: The text traces the history of Brazil's school incentive programs, from the 1990s Bolsa-Escola and Poupança-Escola to their evolution into Bolsa Família and Pé-de-Meia, emphasizing their role in reducing school dropout rates. However, it critiques the assumption that mere school attendance equals learning, arguing that schools must be enjoyable and useful to truly engage students, preventing both student dropout and institutional disengagement from youth interests. While reduced dropout is positive, it is insufficient without educational quality and relevance to students' lives.

item.title: PL e Flávio acham que não há mais reconciliação com Michelle
item.description: The PL leadership and Flávio Bolsonaro conclude there is no longer any chance of reconciliation with Michelle Bolsonaro before the 2026 elections, viewing the effort as futile after her public statements of rupture. The split removes a key bridge for Flávio to female and evangelical voters, demographics where Michelle had strong influence. According to PoderData/Aya poll, Lula has 45% and Flávio 43% in voting intentions for a potential runoff, technically tied within the margin of error.

item.title: Democracia é irreal no Brasil porque exclui maioria da população
item.description: Lawyer and political scientist Gabriela Rollemberg claims Brazilian democracy is unreal because it excludes the majority of the population, particularly women, who make up 52% of the electorate but hold only 17.7% of congressional seats. She cites the absence of female presidential candidates in 2026 for the first time in 20 years, party amnesties that violate gender and racial quotas, gender-based violence in politics, and the neglect of care policies like childcare and full-time education as key barriers to women's political advancement.

item.title: Só mulheres são capazes de romper a polarização, diz Gabriela Rollemberg
item.description: Lawyer and political scientist Gabriela Rollemberg stated that the female vote will be decisive in the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections and that women are the only force capable of reducing political polarization. She noted that, despite representing 52% of the electorate, women hold only 17.7% of congressional seats due to historical barriers and ineffective enforcement of gender quotas. Rollemberg urged women to scrutinize candidates’ proposals on security, childcare, full-time education, and the care economy.

item.title: O que a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro espera de Tarcísio no primeiro turno
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign would like to receive a strong endorsement from Tarcísio de Freitas in the first round of the 2026 presidential election, but does not expect it to happen. The article notes that while the campaign desires such support, it acknowledges the difficulty of securing a clear endorsement from the São Paulo governor. The content is exclusive to subscribers and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Fala de Flávio reforça tese de Michelle, dizem aliados da ex-primeira-dama
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro stated he no longer has a relationship with Michelle Bolsonaro, confirming her prior remarks about her stepson. Allies of the former first lady interpreted this as confirmation of her position. The statement was made amid the 2026 presidential pre-campaign context.

item.title: Articulação por vice isola Flávio e aumenta tensão entre aliados
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's effort to nominate Daniella Marques as his vice-presidential running mate is seen as a dangerous misstep by PL allies and centrist parties, who fear it will isolate the candidate and heighten internal tensions. The choice is criticized for lacking political and strategic alignment, causing friction among supporters. The move is viewed as a threat to ticket cohesion and electoral viability in 2026.

item.title: Bater ou não bater: Dilema de Flávio nas pesquisas impõe desafio a rivais
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) presidential campaign in 2026 is facing stagnation in the polls amid a series of crises, creating a strategic dilemma for his rivals on the right and center-right: whether to attack him or not, weighing the risk of energizing his base against fragmenting the opposition. The core question is whether direct confrontation would benefit opponents or inadvertently boost Bolsonarism.

item.title: Ascensão de Trump fez gestão Lula retomar diálogo com os EUA sobre cooperação em defesa e segurança
item.description: The Lula administration sought to resume defense and security cooperation with the United States, even after Trump designated the PCC and CV as terrorist organizations in June 2025. Despite the measure causing tensions and halting correspondence for five days, officials from both countries continued dialogue efforts, including a meeting between Brazilian Defense Minister José Múcio and U.S. Undersecretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby in Peru to discuss narcotics trafficking. The Brazilian government viewed the U.S. measure as a threat to sovereignty but insists on dialogue to advance bilateral agreements.

item.title: O valor bilionário que Joesley Batista quer para vender à Vale mina comprada em 2022
item.description: Joesley Batista, owner of J&F, is seeking to sell back to Vale a mine acquired in 2022 for a billion-dollar amount, despite internal Vale assessments indicating the deal is not advantageous. The proposal sparked controversy within Vale’s board after leaked emails revealed secret visits by board members to the mine and a dinner between Vale executives and J&F owners. The move is seen as an attempt to secure financial gain tied to Batista’s close relationship with President Lula.

item.title: Com novo tarifaço de Trump e déficit fiscal crescente, Brasil chega à eleição mais importante do mundo em 2026 sem margem para erro, diz analista
item.description: Global strategist Ruchir Sharma warns that Trump's new tariff hikes and Brazil's rising fiscal deficit create a highly complex scenario for the 2026 elections, leaving little room for error and affecting both foreign investment and the domestic political landscape.

item.title: Flávio recorre a estilo usado por Nikolas para chamar atenção em vídeo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) used a camera-tapping gesture popularized by Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) in a video criticizing the new U.S. tariffs on Brazil and blaming Lula. The tactic, aimed at boosting social media engagement, was acknowledged by Nikolas in the comments. The move comes as allies pressure Flávio to increase his online presence, a domain where Nikolas is seen as a benchmark.

item.title: Lula costura candidaturas ao Senado próximo ao prazo para convenções
item.description: President Lula is coordinating Senate candidacies to strengthen the governing base and prevent an opposition majority in the 2026 elections. In Ceará, he secured Cid Gomes' (PSB) re-election bid, who will run alongside Elmano de Freitas (PT), while his brother Ciro Gomes (PSDB) is expected to run for governor with PL support. In Mato Grosso do Sul, Lula confirmed backing for Senator Soraya Thronicke's (PSB) re-election, who is now allied with Vander Loubet (PT) in the race.

item.title: Celina diz que vai trabalhar para que Michelle Bolsonaro concorra ao Senado
item.description: The governor of the Federal District, Celina Leão (PP), stated she will work to ensure Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) runs for the Senate in 2026, calling her an important asset and poll leader. She also confirmed Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) as her presidential candidate, with whom she is allied, and noted Ibaneis Rocha’s (MDB) withdrawal from the Senate race as a personal decision.

item.title: Fim da 6x1: Senado inicia recesso e impõe derrota a calendário de Lula
item.description: Lula's government failed to pass in the Senate the PEC to reduce the workweek from 44 to 40 hours (end of the 6x1), already approved by the Chamber. Senate President Davi Alcolumbre kept the proposal stalled, citing the need for careful deliberation and holding meetings with business and union leaders. The measure, which includes a two-stage transition and wage protection, remains shelved during the parliamentary recess.

item.title: SP Gastronomia 2026 abre a venda de ingressos hoje; conheça as atrações
item.description: SP Gastronomia 2026 opens ticket sales today at 10 a.m. for events on August 21–23 and 28–30 at Parque Villa-Lobos. The festival features over 20 renowned São Paulo restaurants, including A Casa do Porco, Muli, and Grand Hyatt São Paulo, plus daily shows with artists like Péricles and Ferrugem, offering a global culinary journey with Middle Eastern, Brazilian, and European-inspired dishes.

item.title: Tarifaço: a conexão Trump-Bolsonaro que custa bilhões ao Brasil
item.description: The United States has imposed a new 25% tariff on Brazilian products including sugarcane ethanol, gasoline, and heavy machinery, allegedly to influence Brazil’s 2026 presidential election in favor of Flávio Bolsonaro. This move, part of Trump’s aggressive trade policy, revives historical tariff conflicts but now carries a clear political-electoral motive. While key Brazilian exports like orange juice, beef, and aircraft were exempted, the measure still inflicts significant economic harm and is widely interpreted as an attempt at foreign interference in Brazil’s democratic process.
